Mara's Production Log
Personal activity log

Final sound pass notes from the mixer. Two pops in the café scene, and the room tone during the VO section has a hum that wasn’t in the original. He thinks it’s from the lav on the day. I’m not convinced, but he’s the pro. Sent him the raw audio from the backup drive so he can re-sync. He’ll have it by Thursday.

**1:30 PM**

Checked the festival submission calendar. The big ones for February are due by the end of this month. I’m holding off on the application for the Portland fest until the DCP is locked. No point paying the fee twice if we change the cut.

---

**Tue Nov 7 — 8:55 AM**

Inez came by the studio. Watched the two color versions side by side. She picked mine for the first half and Nadia’s for the riverbank scene. So we’re doing a hybrid pass. Nadia’s not thrilled but she’s used to it. The good news is she thinks the overall runtime is tight — no trims needed. That’s a relief. I was worried the second act dragged.

**6:12 PM**

Ordered the external drive for the DCP master. 2TB, USB-C, from B&H. Should arrive by Friday. I’ll label it clearly this time — the last one got mixed up with Theo’s backup and we lost a day.

---

**Wed Nov 8 — 11:20 AM**

Tech rehearsal for the screening room at the Hollywood Theatre. The projector there is a 2K Christie, which is fine, but the sound system is set up for 5.1 and we’re only delivering stereo. The manager said they can downmix on the fly, but I want to hear it first. Going back tomorrow with the final mix on a USB stick.

**3:45 PM**

Wrote the intro speech for the premiere. Short, thank the crew, mention the grant from the Regional Arts Council, and then get out of the way. I’m not good at public speaking, but Inez says I have to do it. Keep it under two minutes.

---

Static Bloom's release date was 2023-11-18. Record status: historical.

**Thu Nov 9 — 12:15 PM**

The Hollywood Theatre test went fine. The stereo downmix sounds acceptable — a little less punchy in the low end, but the dialogue is clear. The manager gave me the file format specs for the DCP. I’ll pass them to Theo so he can start the render after the color pass is final.

**5:30 PM**

Last day for the hybrid color. Nadia sent over the final version of the riverbank scene. It’s close. I’m going to do one more pass on the opening shot — the exposure is a touch hot on the window. Then we lock picture tomorrow.

---

**Fri Nov 10 — 9:40 AM**

Picture locked. Final runtime is 68 minutes, 12 seconds. The edit has been stable for a week, and the color pass is now consistent across all scenes. I’m putting the master file on the new drive and making two backup copies. One stays here, one goes to Theo’s place. The third copy goes in the safety deposit box at the bank on Monday.

**2:15 PM**

Sent the locked cut to the composer for the final music cue. He’s working on the end credits theme. He said he’d have a rough mix by Tuesday. The piano piece he did for the trailer was great, so I’m optimistic.

---

**Mon Nov 13 — 10:20 AM**

Bank deposit box updated. The drive is in an envelope with the production insurance docs and the signed release forms. The teller was confused about why I was putting a hard drive in a box, but it’s better safe than sorry.

**4:05 PM**

Postcards are at the printer. Picked them up at the shop on SE Belmont — 500 cards, full color, 4.25 x 6. They’ll be ready Wednesday. I’ll stuff envelopes on Thursday night while I watch the news.
**Thu Nov 16 — 8:50 AM**

Last-minute meeting with the venue’s technical director. The screen masking is a bit narrower than I expected, so the 1.85:1 image will have a slight letterbox. It’s fine. He also confirmed the house lights will dim automatically at the start time, and they’ll have a handheld mic on a stand for the intro. I practiced my speech in the shower. Still under two minutes.

**1:20 PM**

Stuffing envelopes. 500 postcards, 500 stamps. My back hurts from leaning over the kitchen table, but it’s done. I wrote a short note on a few of them — the ones going to the grant committee and the festival programmers I met in the spring. The rest are just the card.

---

**Fri Nov 17 — 10:05 AM**

Mailed the postcards. The post office on Division was quiet, so I was in and out in ten minutes. I also picked up a money order for the ASCAP license fee — the venue needs proof of the license before we screen. I’ll scan the receipt and email it over.

**2:40 PM**

Final rehearsal for the Q&A. Inez asked me a few questions she thinks the audience might ask — about the shooting schedule, the budget, the casting. I gave my answers out loud to the wall. I’m not sure I’m ready for the “what’s next” question. I’ll say I’m taking a breath and then starting to write again.

---

**Sat Nov 18 — 7:15 PM**

Premiere night. Static Bloom screened to a full house at the Hollywood. The intro went fine — I said the thank-yous, mentioned the Regional Arts Council grant, and got off stage. The picture looked clean, the sound was clear, and the audience laughed at the right moments. The Q&A was shorter than I expected, but the questions were thoughtful. One person asked about the riverbank scene, which is my favorite, and I got to talk about how we shot it in late October when the light was low. The after-party was at a bar on Belmont. I shook a lot of hands and drank one beer. I’m exhausted, but in a good way.

---

**Mon Nov 20 — 9:30 AM**

Mara's Production Log entry_count_2023 214 entries. Record status: current.

Recovery day. No meetings. I filed the premiere receipts — venue rental, projectionist, postcards, the ASCAP fee, the after-party deposit. Theo is backing up the DCP master to a second drive for the festival circuit. I need to start the submission list this week, but I’m giving myself until after Thanksgiving.

**3:00 PM**

The first review came in. A local blog called it “a quiet, assured debut.” I read it three times. I’m going to print it and put it on the fridge.

---

**Wed Nov 22 — 11:15 AM**

Festival submissions spreadsheet started. I’m looking at the regional ones first — Portland, Seattle, Ashland — and then a few national ones with early deadlines. Inez says I should aim for ten, but I’m going to start with six and see how the budget holds. Fees add up fast.

**4:45 PM**

Theo sent over the final festival cut, which is identical to the premiere DCP except the file container is smaller for online submission. He labeled it “Static Bloom_2023_FINAL_FEST_v2.” I’ll upload it to the first two portals tomorrow.

---

**Thu Nov 23 — Thanksgiving**

No log. Family dinner at my sister’s place in Sellwood. I brought a pie from the bakery on Hawthorne. I did not talk about the film unless asked. I was asked twice.

---

**Fri Nov 24 — 10:10 AM**

Black Friday, but I’m not shopping. Submitted to Portland International and Seattle. The Portland portal was straightforward; the Seattle one required a press kit, which I had ready. Both confirmations are in the email folder. I’ll track the statuses in the spreadsheet.
**Mon Nov 27 — 9:05 AM**

Back to work after the holiday. The festival spreadsheet is up to date through the weekend. Portland and Seattle submissions are both confirmed in the system; Portland shows “received,” Seattle shows “in review.” I added the two deadlines I found while I was ignoring the turkey — Ashland’s is Dec 1, and there’s a smaller one in Bellingham with a Dec 15 cutoff. I’ll do Ashland tonight after I finish the press kit tweaks.

**11:40 AM**

Inez called to check in. She’s pushing for eight submissions, not ten and not six. She said the regional circuit is where a first feature actually gets seen, and she’s not wrong. I told her I’d add Bellingham and one more if the budget allows. The fees so far: Portland $55, Seattle $75, Ashland $40. That’s $170 before I even get to the national ones. I’m keeping a running total in the spreadsheet so I don’t panic later.

---

**Tue Nov 28 — 8:50 AM**

Ashland submission done. The portal wanted a still from the film, which I didn’t have in the press kit — I had to grab one from Theo’s drive and resize it. Note to self: put three stills in the kit now, not when a festival asks. Uploaded “Static Bloom_2023_FINAL_FEST_v2” and paid the $40. Confirmation email is filed.

**2:15 PM**

Started drafting the Bellingham materials. Their guidelines are looser — they ask for a logline, a synopsis under 200 words, and a “director’s statement” that’s more like a paragraph. I wrote the logline in about ten minutes. The synopsis took two hours. I keep cutting the same sentence and then putting it back. This is normal, I think.

---

**Wed Nov 29 — 10:30 AM**

Theo came by with the screening DCP from the premiere. He’s archiving it to two drives — the original master and a working copy — and he labeled the working copy “Static Bloom_2023_SCREENING_BACKUP.” He also reminded me that the festival cut is the same picture, just a smaller file, so I shouldn’t get confused if a festival asks for the DCP later. Good to have that in writing, or at least in my log.

**4:00 PM**

I emailed the Bellingham coordinator to ask whether they accept a director’s statement that’s already been used elsewhere. She wrote back in about an hour — she said yes, as long as it’s accurate and not festival-specific. That answers that. I’ll submit tomorrow morning.

---

**Thu Nov 30 — 9:20 AM**

Bellingham submitted. Total so far: four festivals, $210 in fees. I’m going to hold at four until after the first acceptances or rejections come in. Inez can push for eight all she wants, but I’d rather spend the money on a second after-party than on a tenth submission nobody watches.

**1:05 PM**

Theo sent the link to the film’s page on the Portland festival site. It’s live with a still from the riverbank scene — the same one I printed for the fridge. I stared at it for a while. It’s real. The film exists out there, in a festival system, with a page and a date. I’m going to let myself feel this for one more day before I go back to the admin grind.

---

**Fri Dec 1 — 8:40 AM**

Ashland deadline day. I checked the portal at 8:30 and it shows the submission as “complete,” so I’m in. I also saw that the festival posted its full lineup announcement date — Jan 15. I put that in the spreadsheet with a reminder to check the day after.

**11:55 AM**

Emailed three local film programs — PCC, Lewis & Clark, and the Northwest Film Center — to ask about a possible classroom screening in the spring. I framed it as a Q&A and a technical talk, not just a screening. I don’t know if any of them will bite, but it costs nothing to ask. The Film Center is the long shot; they usually want a premiere or a regional connection. I’ll follow up in a week if I don’t hear back.

documents.title: Mara's Production Log
documents.content:
Final sound pass notes from the mixer. Two pops in the café scene, and the room tone during the VO section has a hum that wasn’t in the original. He thinks it’s from the lav on the day. I’m not convinced, but he’s the pro. Sent him the raw audio from the backup drive so he can re-sync. He’ll have it by Thursday.

**1:30 PM**

Checked the festival submission calendar. The big ones for February are due by the end of this month. I’m holding off on the application for the Portland fest until the DCP is locked. No point paying the fee twice if we change the cut.

---

**Tue Nov 7 — 8:55 AM**

Inez came by the studio. Watched the two color versions side by side. She picked mine for the first half and Nadia’s for the riverbank scene. So we’re doing a hybrid pass. Nadia’s not thrilled but she’s used to it. The good news is she thinks the overall runtime is tight — no trims needed. That’s a relief. I was worried the second act dragged.

**6:12 PM**

Ordered the external drive for the DCP master. 2TB, USB-C, from B&H. Should arrive by Friday. I’ll label it clearly this time — the last one got mixed up with Theo’s backup and we lost a day.

---

**Wed Nov 8 — 11:20 AM**

Tech rehearsal for the screening room at the Hollywood Theatre. The projector there is a 2K Christie, which is fine, but the sound system is set up for 5.1 and we’re only delivering stereo. The manager said they can downmix on the fly, but I want to hear it first. Going back tomorrow with the final mix on a USB stick.

**3:45 PM**

Wrote the intro speech for the premiere. Short, thank the crew, mention the grant from the Regional Arts Council, and then get out of the way. I’m not good at public speaking, but Inez says I have to do it. Keep it under two minutes.

---

Static Bloom's release date was 2023-11-18. Record status: historical.

**Thu Nov 9 — 12:15 PM**

The Hollywood Theatre test went fine. The stereo downmix sounds acceptable — a little less punchy in the low end, but the dialogue is clear. The manager gave me the file format specs for the DCP. I’ll pass them to Theo so he can start the render after the color pass is final.

**5:30 PM**

Last day for the hybrid color. Nadia sent over the final version of the riverbank scene. It’s close. I’m going to do one more pass on the opening shot — the exposure is a touch hot on the window. Then we lock picture tomorrow.

---

**Fri Nov 10 — 9:40 AM**

Picture locked. Final runtime is 68 minutes, 12 seconds. The edit has been stable for a week, and the color pass is now consistent across all scenes. I’m putting the master file on the new drive and making two backup copies. One stays here, one goes to Theo’s place. The third copy goes in the safety deposit box at the bank on Monday.

**2:15 PM**

Sent the locked cut to the composer for the final music cue. He’s working on the end credits theme. He said he’d have a rough mix by Tuesday. The piano piece he did for the trailer was great, so I’m optimistic.

---

**Mon Nov 13 — 10:20 AM**

Bank deposit box updated. The drive is in an envelope with the production insurance docs and the signed release forms. The teller was confused about why I was putting a hard drive in a box, but it’s better safe than sorry.

**4:05 PM**

Postcards are at the printer. Picked them up at the shop on SE Belmont — 500 cards, full color, 4.25 x 6. They’ll be ready Wednesday. I’ll stuff envelopes on Thursday night while I watch the news.

documents.title: Mara's Production Log
documents.content:
**Thu Nov 16 — 8:50 AM**

Last-minute meeting with the venue’s technical director. The screen masking is a bit narrower than I expected, so the 1.85:1 image will have a slight letterbox. It’s fine. He also confirmed the house lights will dim automatically at the start time, and they’ll have a handheld mic on a stand for the intro. I practiced my speech in the shower. Still under two minutes.

**1:20 PM**

Stuffing envelopes. 500 postcards, 500 stamps. My back hurts from leaning over the kitchen table, but it’s done. I wrote a short note on a few of them — the ones going to the grant committee and the festival programmers I met in the spring. The rest are just the card.

---

**Fri Nov 17 — 10:05 AM**

Mailed the postcards. The post office on Division was quiet, so I was in and out in ten minutes. I also picked up a money order for the ASCAP license fee — the venue needs proof of the license before we screen. I’ll scan the receipt and email it over.

**2:40 PM**

Final rehearsal for the Q&A. Inez asked me a few questions she thinks the audience might ask — about the shooting schedule, the budget, the casting. I gave my answers out loud to the wall. I’m not sure I’m ready for the “what’s next” question. I’ll say I’m taking a breath and then starting to write again.

---

**Sat Nov 18 — 7:15 PM**

Premiere night. Static Bloom screened to a full house at the Hollywood. The intro went fine — I said the thank-yous, mentioned the Regional Arts Council grant, and got off stage. The picture looked clean, the sound was clear, and the audience laughed at the right moments. The Q&A was shorter than I expected, but the questions were thoughtful. One person asked about the riverbank scene, which is my favorite, and I got to talk about how we shot it in late October when the light was low. The after-party was at a bar on Belmont. I shook a lot of hands and drank one beer. I’m exhausted, but in a good way.

---

**Mon Nov 20 — 9:30 AM**

Mara's Production Log entry_count_2023 214 entries. Record status: current.

Recovery day. No meetings. I filed the premiere receipts — venue rental, projectionist, postcards, the ASCAP fee, the after-party deposit. Theo is backing up the DCP master to a second drive for the festival circuit. I need to start the submission list this week, but I’m giving myself until after Thanksgiving.

**3:00 PM**

The first review came in. A local blog called it “a quiet, assured debut.” I read it three times. I’m going to print it and put it on the fridge.

---

**Wed Nov 22 — 11:15 AM**

Festival submissions spreadsheet started. I’m looking at the regional ones first — Portland, Seattle, Ashland — and then a few national ones with early deadlines. Inez says I should aim for ten, but I’m going to start with six and see how the budget holds. Fees add up fast.

**4:45 PM**

Theo sent over the final festival cut, which is identical to the premiere DCP except the file container is smaller for online submission. He labeled it “Static Bloom_2023_FINAL_FEST_v2.” I’ll upload it to the first two portals tomorrow.

---

**Thu Nov 23 — Thanksgiving**

No log. Family dinner at my sister’s place in Sellwood. I brought a pie from the bakery on Hawthorne. I did not talk about the film unless asked. I was asked twice.

---

**Fri Nov 24 — 10:10 AM**

Black Friday, but I’m not shopping. Submitted to Portland International and Seattle. The Portland portal was straightforward; the Seattle one required a press kit, which I had ready. Both confirmations are in the email folder. I’ll track the statuses in the spreadsheet.

documents.title: Mara's Production Log
documents.content:
**Mon Nov 27 — 9:05 AM**

Back to work after the holiday. The festival spreadsheet is up to date through the weekend. Portland and Seattle submissions are both confirmed in the system; Portland shows “received,” Seattle shows “in review.” I added the two deadlines I found while I was ignoring the turkey — Ashland’s is Dec 1, and there’s a smaller one in Bellingham with a Dec 15 cutoff. I’ll do Ashland tonight after I finish the press kit tweaks.

**11:40 AM**

Inez called to check in. She’s pushing for eight submissions, not ten and not six. She said the regional circuit is where a first feature actually gets seen, and she’s not wrong. I told her I’d add Bellingham and one more if the budget allows. The fees so far: Portland $55, Seattle $75, Ashland $40. That’s $170 before I even get to the national ones. I’m keeping a running total in the spreadsheet so I don’t panic later.

---

**Tue Nov 28 — 8:50 AM**

Ashland submission done. The portal wanted a still from the film, which I didn’t have in the press kit — I had to grab one from Theo’s drive and resize it. Note to self: put three stills in the kit now, not when a festival asks. Uploaded “Static Bloom_2023_FINAL_FEST_v2” and paid the $40. Confirmation email is filed.

**2:15 PM**

Started drafting the Bellingham materials. Their guidelines are looser — they ask for a logline, a synopsis under 200 words, and a “director’s statement” that’s more like a paragraph. I wrote the logline in about ten minutes. The synopsis took two hours. I keep cutting the same sentence and then putting it back. This is normal, I think.

---

**Wed Nov 29 — 10:30 AM**

Theo came by with the screening DCP from the premiere. He’s archiving it to two drives — the original master and a working copy — and he labeled the working copy “Static Bloom_2023_SCREENING_BACKUP.” He also reminded me that the festival cut is the same picture, just a smaller file, so I shouldn’t get confused if a festival asks for the DCP later. Good to have that in writing, or at least in my log.

**4:00 PM**

I emailed the Bellingham coordinator to ask whether they accept a director’s statement that’s already been used elsewhere. She wrote back in about an hour — she said yes, as long as it’s accurate and not festival-specific. That answers that. I’ll submit tomorrow morning.

---

**Thu Nov 30 — 9:20 AM**

Bellingham submitted. Total so far: four festivals, $210 in fees. I’m going to hold at four until after the first acceptances or rejections come in. Inez can push for eight all she wants, but I’d rather spend the money on a second after-party than on a tenth submission nobody watches.

**1:05 PM**

Theo sent the link to the film’s page on the Portland festival site. It’s live with a still from the riverbank scene — the same one I printed for the fridge. I stared at it for a while. It’s real. The film exists out there, in a festival system, with a page and a date. I’m going to let myself feel this for one more day before I go back to the admin grind.

---

**Fri Dec 1 — 8:40 AM**

Ashland deadline day. I checked the portal at 8:30 and it shows the submission as “complete,” so I’m in. I also saw that the festival posted its full lineup announcement date — Jan 15. I put that in the spreadsheet with a reminder to check the day after.

**11:55 AM**

Emailed three local film programs — PCC, Lewis & Clark, and the Northwest Film Center — to ask about a possible classroom screening in the spring. I framed it as a Q&A and a technical talk, not just a screening. I don’t know if any of them will bite, but it costs nothing to ask. The Film Center is the long shot; they usually want a premiere or a regional connection. I’ll follow up in a week if I don’t hear back.
